tier_reason: Public benchmark code (test/bench_read.cpp, test/bench_write.cpp, test/CMakeLists.txt, docs/benchmark/run_benchmarks.sh) plus raw Google Benchmark logs, run directly against RapidJSON. The page states GCC 15.2.0, -O3 -march=x86-64-v3 with LTO (confirmed in test/CMakeLists.txt), and an Intel Core i9-12900K.

corrections.claimed_speedup: vs RapidJSON: 1.4-4.6x faster reads, 2.6-8.1x faster writes across the ten documents (per-document ranges from the root README table); time-weighted totals: 2.31x faster reads, 3.91x faster writes (docs/benchmark page). vs simdjson: 1.1-1.6x faster reads against On Demand on read-only input including copy+pad (root README range); the weighted 2.14x is against simdjson DOM, and against On Demand on a caller-prepared padded buffer the weighted margin is 1.34x fresh / 1.19x with parser and allocator reused (simdjson has no serializer). vs nlohmann-json: 2.8-27x faster writes, weighted 6.67x (not in read comparison). vs upstream yyjson: 1.0-1.8x faster reads / 1.0-2.1x faster writes, weighted 1.69x / 1.46x.
corrections.caveats: The project's own README flags an asymmetry as the main caveat of its comparison: simdjson and yyjson are linked as prebuilt vcpkg libraries without -march=x86-64-v3 or LTO, while header-only rapidjson and nlohmann-json get the same flags as cpp-yyjson; this could inflate the margin against simdjson/yyjson specifically (simdjson picks SIMD kernels at runtime, which partly offsets this). The page also says much of the weighted total comes from the bundled backend's madvise(MADV_HUGEPAGE) on >32 MiB blocks (Linux/glibc only), which only the two large documents (fgo, otfcc) get; with the allocator reused the fgo/otfcc read margin over yyjson shrinks to 91%/96% of its time. The per-document ranges come from the root README table; the weighted totals come from docs/benchmark/README.md. I recomputed both from the committed raw logs and they match. Compiler, flags and CPU are stated, and the code and raw logs are public, so Tier A holds.

notes: I recomputed every ratio from the committed logs (test/*_bench_*.log): RapidJSON read 1.40-4.58x (weighted 2.31), write 2.56-8.11x (3.91); nlohmann 2.77-26.7x (6.67); yyjson read 1.05-1.79x (1.69), write 0.99-2.11x (1.46); simdjson On Demand copy+pad 1.06-1.65x, DOM weighted 2.14x. The only fix is in claimed_speedup: the record had attached the weighted 2.14x to the On Demand range, but 2.14x is against DOM. Metadata checks out (MIT, 95 stars, last commit 2026-09-24, v1.0.0 release, not a fork, not archived).

tier_reason: First-party README numbers against RapidJSON (DOM plus manual populate, or hand-written SAX), with public code (benchmarks/syntetic/, benchmarks/twitter_json/, benchmarks/canada_json/). The README never states optimization flags or build type, and the twitter.json and canada.json runs name no CPU model, so this is partial methodology and cannot be A.

corrections.claimed_speedup: vs RapidJSON + manual mapping (parse+validate+populate): ~same speed on static embedded config (vs hand-written SAX), 40% faster dynamic embedded config, 20% faster telemetry, 65% faster RPC commands, 15% faster log events, 20% faster bus events, 15% faster metrics; about 1.5x faster on twitter.json (1020 vs 1620 microseconds/iter). On canada.json it is ~15% slower than RapidJSON for parse-and-populate and ~80% slower than hand-written RapidJSON SAX for typed streaming; only with selective field-skipping (float parsing skipped) is it ~60% faster than hand-written RapidJSON SAX.
corrections.hardware: Apple M1 Max, macOS 26.1 (6-scenario benchmark); arm64 Ubuntu Linux 24.04 machine, CPU model not stated (twitter.json benchmark); canada.json hardware not stated
corrections.compiler_and_flags: GCC 14 (6-scenario benchmark), GCC 14.3 (twitter.json benchmark); canada.json compiler not stated. The README states no optimization flags or build type. The repo CMakeLists.txt adds -flto=8 -ffunction-sections -fdata-sections (plus -fno-exceptions -fno-rtti on the synthetic and canada targets) only in the Release config.
corrections.caveats: First-party README benchmark. The CPU model is given for one table only (M1 Max), and neither table gives optimization flags or build type, so methodology is only partly specified. Mixed results: on canada.json it is ~15% slower than RapidJSON parse+populate and ~80% slower than RapidJSON SAX in typed streaming, and the ~60% win needs skip annotations that avoid float parsing entirely, so it is not equal work. The README says Glaze is ~3x faster on twitter.json. The README's benchmark links (benchmarks/main.cpp, benchmarks/canada_json_parsing.cpp) are stale; the code now lives in benchmarks/syntetic/ and benchmarks/canada_json/. A very young, low-star project, recently added to vcpkg; the numbers are self-reported and have not been reproduced independently.

notes: All claimed numbers appear in the README's Parsing Speed section and its twitter.json table (1620/1020 = 1.59x; the page says 'about 1.5x'). The record left out the canada.json losses, so I added them to claimed_speedup. Metadata checks out (MIT, 15 stars, last commit 2026-08-06, not a fork, not archived).
